# Coordinated recovery and bounded sent-history custody

Status: selected and qualified for the bounded Q04 component; full endpoint and native other-OS gates remain open.

Add a separate pure packet-space owner; preserve recovery.Initial and its public semantics. Three bounded histories share one RTT estimator, PTO backoff and byte-flight ledger. Frame retransmission custody remains with the host: opaque tokens in copied ACK/loss/discard outcomes identify its retained work. Register only known successful sends after preflight; encryption reservations remain a separate owner and cannot be reused after a failed send.

Use monotonically increasing actual-send ordinals, not numeric PN differences, for the threshold of three later sends. RFC 9002 A.10 explicitly states that its subtraction assumes no sender-induced gaps. This preserves the existing local rule and must be checked against independent dense/sparse peer traces. Ordinals survive slot reclamation and Retry; distinct spaces never share ACK or loss history. RTT and bytes in flight are path-wide. No migration or congestion-window algorithm is introduced by this component.

D07: retain at most P packet entries per space. Before a new send, evict only a contiguous prefix of acknowledged, declared-lost, Retry-discarded, or non-flight/no-retransmission entries. Never evict active flight. Advance an exclusive ACK-validation floor past each evicted PN. Validate every claimed number at/above this floor against retained actual sends, including gaps; ignore the portion below the floor. Reject ACK above the lifetime highest successful send. Reclaimed lost originals cannot later acknowledge shared frame data; the host continues recovery through retained/retransmitted tokens. Within the horizon a late original ACK returns its token exactly once with zero second flight debit. This is an explicit bounded late-ACK policy, not lifetime proof of every sent number.

Each operation returns a bounded copied outcome batch; no callbacks or allocations occur. The caller must consume outcomes before another mutation. All rejected send/ACK/time/lifecycle preflights preserve state. Whole packet multi-frame transactions are still Q07; checkAck followed by receiveAck is safe only with serialized unchanged state and complete outer admission.

Only Application ACK delay is decoded (exponent at most 20); ignore it for Initial/Handshake. Before confirmation, use uncapped delay when plausible; after confirmation cap to negotiated max_ack_delay. First sample ignores delay, min RTT uses raw elapsed; later weighted variance uses the old smoothed RTT as in RFC 9002 A.7 and the existing Initial helper. Rounded loss delay is ceiling(9*max(latest,smoothed)/8), minimum 1000us. Intermediate arithmetic is widened.

One next timer: earliest loss deadline takes precedence over any PTO; ties use Initial, Handshake, Application order. Application PTO is disabled until confirmation; PTO requests one pending eliciting probe without declaring loss. A pending probe suppresses repeated PTO events, but loss deadlines remain serviceable. Host amplification blocking suppresses server PTO, not time-loss accounting. A client has an anchored anti-deadlock PTO until a Handshake ACK or confirmation proves server validation. Polling cannot extend the anchor. Key discard resets PTO backoff and debits flight once without reporting congestion loss. Retry is client-only/once/before authenticated peer progress; reset RTT/recovery and discard Initial packet effects while preserving consumed PN/ordinal history and returning tokens for host requeue.

Clock rollback fails before mutation. Deadline arithmetic returns TimeExhausted rather than wrapping or indefinitely saturating; the connection host must cancel/close on that outcome. Repeated cancel/discard must not release bytes twice. All storage and returned batches have compile-time bounded sizes; no claims about TLS-provider or whole-connection memory.

The outer owner decides idle expiry before dispatching recovery work. cancel returns discard effects and suppresses all timers; timeout after cancellation fails without reviving a probe. This component does not itself implement an idle clock. Actual key discard reanchors client anti-deadlock once; repeated discard does not postpone it. Repeated handshake confirmation cannot reset PTO backoff. noteAuthenticatedPeerPacket records admitted non-ACK progress so Retry cannot reopen the initial flight afterward.

Required tests: equal deadlines, loss-before-PTO, all three spaces/ACK isolation, padded ACK byte accounting, confirmation and plausible/clamped ACK delays, dense/sparse packet threshold, exact time boundaries, late original ACK, reclamation/gap/horizon behavior, many capacity cycles, resource rollback, Retry and old ACKs, no-busy-spin probes, anti-amplification/unblocking, clock/PTO overflow, idempotent discard/cancel, external consumer and both native modes plus pure cross targets.

Standards: [RFC 9002 recovery](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9002.html#appendix-A.10), [RFC 9000 ACK validation](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html#section-13.1). Independent component reference: [pinned quic-go history](https://github.com/quic-go/quic-go/blob/816f839038f72256fa7b7a971f64cc7411f0f426/internal/ackhandler/sent_packet_history.go). Its four-skipped-number retention bounds the peer comparison cases; the local ordinal policy also covers larger gaps with separate mathematical tests.
